why: Both chat entry points await _extract_user_facts with the user message and session id before delegation (module.py:105, 160); the helper awaits ConversationFactExtractor.extract_and_store (module.py:185-187), which calls FactExtractor.extract_from_text (conversation_extractor.py:43) and FactStore.add_fact per fact (conversation_extractor.py:58). main.py injects the real FactStore-backed extractor (main.py:253-255) into ExecutionModule (main.py:295); the API chat routes call that module (src/cortex/api/routes/chat.py:82,149). Ran: uv run pytest tests/memory/test_conversation_extractor.py tests/memory/test_fact_extractor.py tests/unit/test_execution_module_extraction.py -q -> 43 passed; ruff check and mypy on the changed source files pass. Supplied live fake-LLM check (not re-run by me): 3 facts stored with source/session payloads. Caveat: initialize_app is not unit-tested (needs Postgres/migrations), so the composition-root wiring is inspection+mypy only; no real provider call was made.

quote: "- static: irrefutable, never-changing statements (birth date or place, native language, "
why: The prompt defines static as 'irrefutable, never-changing statements (birth date or place, native language, immutable identity)' and asks for a mutability on every fact (fact_extractor.py:20-25). The parser maps the field through FactMutability and pins confidence at 1.0 for STATIC (fact_extractor.py:84-91), and the Fact carries that mutability (fact_extractor.py:97). Tests: test_extract_from_text_marks_irrefutable_statement_static and test_static_mutability_forces_confidence_to_one. Advisory: the classification is entirely LLM judgment; there is no allow-list tying STATIC to identity/user_fact types, so a misclassified preference can be inserted as an unretractable static fact.

quote: 'Attitudes and behaviors are distinct facts: "likes coffee" and "drinks coffee" must '
why: The prompt tells the model that attitudes and behaviors are distinct facts and requires distinct symbolic_repr values (fact_extractor.py:26-27); the parser preserves separate Fact objects and the extractor stores each via add_fact. Tests: test_attitude_and_behavior_are_distinct_facts (two facts, distinct reprs/types) and test_prompt_requires_mutability_and_separates_attitudes_from_behaviors (substring contract). Advisory: this is prompt-only. No post-parse validation enforces distinct reprs or type separation, and if a real model returned the same symbolic_repr for both, FactStore would collapse the second into an update of the first (fact_store.py:70-85). The supplied live check used a fake LLM that already returned distinct reprs; no real-provider evidence.

                mutability=mutability,

                natural_lang_repr=item.get("natural_lang_repr") or "",

Payload defaults to {} on a non-dict (fact_extractor.py:92-93) and the conversation layer adds source/session. Tests assert type/repr/natural/confidence/payload on the stored facts (test_static_birth_place_fact_is_stored_with_confidence_one, test_attitude_and_behavior_are_distinct_facts).

quote: "Conversation fact extraction failed; no facts stored", exc_info=True
why: Blank text returns [] before any LLM call (conversation_extractor.py:39-40). Extraction errors, including malformed JSON and None/empty content raised by FactExtractor.extract_from_text, are caught and logged with [] returned (conversation_extractor.py:42-48); per-fact storage errors are caught and the remaining facts continue (57-64). Tests cover malformed JSON, None, "", {"facts": []}, extractor exceptions and one-fact storage failure; ran the file -> all pass. A non-dict fact item makes _parse_llm_facts raise, which drops the whole batch rather than storing the valid prefix, but that is the AC's specified 'no facts stored, no crash' behavior.

The prompt documents mutability and its four values and lists it among the required item fields (fact_extractor.py:20-29). The parser goes through FactMutability; missing, unknown and invalid values fall back to MUTABLE, STATIC forces confidence 1.0 after the existing clamp, and the existing type/confidence/payload fallbacks are untouched (fact_extractor.py:74-101). Tests cover missing, 'unknown', static, semi_static, and the prompt contract; ran the fact-extractor tests -> pass. Advisory: matching is exact lowercase ('STATIC' would fall back to mutable), which matches the prompt's spelling.

quote: if not text or not text.strip():
why: Blank text short-circuits (conversation_extractor.py:39-40); extraction is wrapped in try/except Exception and returns [] (42-48); each add_fact is isolated in its own try/except so one storage failure does not drop later facts (50-64); payload gets source=conversation and session_id when supplied (54-56); the class uses the existing FactExtractor.extract_from_text and FactStore.add_fact seams. Tests cover blank text with no LLM call, provider failure, malformed output, one-fact storage failure, empty symbolic_repr skipping, and payload semantics. Advisory: the constructor types against the concrete FactExtractor, not cortex.memory.interfaces.FactExtractor that MinionService uses, so an alternative implementation of the seam would not type-check; provenance is set with setdefault, so an LLM-supplied payload source/session_id wins (test_existing_payload_keys_are_not_overwritten pins this), and payload.session_id also changes context relevance scoring (context_provider.py:231-233). Evidence value is symbolic_repr per the evidence spec, so this annotation does not change the value hash.

Both entry points call _extract_user_facts before delegating (module.py:105, 160); the helper is a no-op without an injected extractor and catches any Exception with a warning (176-191), so extraction cannot break chat. main.py injects the extractor into ExecutionModule (main.py:295). run_goal and goal tasks never call it, and only the user message is passed. Stream contract: extraction runs inside the async generator before the loop stream is created and before the first event is yielded; the events themselves are unchanged (test_stream_chat_extracts_before_the_stream_starts, test_stream_chat_survives_an_extraction_failure). Advisory: every chat turn now makes a synchronous extraction LLM call before the loop (plus eager embedding calls inside FactStore.add_fact), with no config/settings switch and no timeout of its own; the stream's docstring still calls the method a 'transparent passthrough' (module.py:128-143) although it now performs this side channel, and docs/specs/architecture.md:146-147 and docs/specs/agentic-loop.md:120-122 still show EX->>L with no extraction step.

On the normal insert path, the parser sets mutability=STATIC and confidence 1.0 (fact_extractor.py:84-101), and PostgresFactRepository.store persists the mutability column (repository.py:67-75), so a new static fact is stored as static at 1.0. The prompt is the only mechanism for attitudes vs behaviors, and the extracted Fact fields match sensory facts. Measured gap: FactStore.add_fact gates on the EXISTING fact's mutability and its update dict omits mutability (fact_store.py:70-81), so when the LLM emits a static fact whose symbolic_repr already exists as non-static, the row is updated with confidence 1.0 and the new payload but keeps its old mutability. I ran FactStore.add_fact with a MagicMock FactRepository: incoming STATIC over an existing MUTABLE row called update(..., {'natural_lang_repr': ..., 'payload': ..., 'confidence': 1.0}) and returned a fact whose mutability was still 'mutable'. The static marking is therefore lost on that path and the 1.0 is not pinned; a later non-static observation can overwrite it. Existing static facts are protected. This is a narrow dedup interaction, not the primary insert path; cross-repr contradictions are explicitly out of scope (#27/#83). Recommend deciding the update rule in #83 or including mutability in the dedup update for a stronger incoming mutability.

quote: > **Status: conversation extraction + STATIC producer (#82) implemented; evidence
why: docs/specs/evidence-system.md:8-12 now says conversation extraction + the STATIC producer (#82) are implemented and the evidence engine (#83) is still designed; it states there is no evidence table and no EvidenceStore, and that facts.confidence is not yet recomputed - all verified by grep over src/ and migrations/. Tests: TestSystemPrompt checks the prompt's mutability/static/attitude contract (tests/memory/test_fact_extractor.py:211-219). Advisory: line 38 still describes a conversation message as 'after #82' (future tense), and the architecture/agentic-loop specs' chat flows do not show the new pre-loop extraction call even though architecture.md:11-15 says the spec is current truth and must be kept in sync. Neither overstates the evidence engine.

quote:
"confidence": (
                        existing.confidence
                        if fact.mutability is FactMutability.STATIC
                        else fact.confidence
                    ),
why: Resolved. The update path now keeps the existing confidence and never writes mutability when the incoming fact is STATIC: updates carries existing.confidence for a static incoming and omits the mutability key (fact_store.py:75-83); the docstring states 'Existing mutability wins' (66-68). The new regression test asserts the exact update dict, '"mutability" not in updates' and result mutability MUTABLE (tests/memory/test_fact_store.py:197-232). Ran the two selected tests -> 2 passed; ran test_fact_store.py + test_conversation_extractor.py + test_fact_extractor.py + test_execution_module_extraction.py -> 57 passed; ruff and mypy on the changed source files pass. I reproduced with FactStore + MagicMock FactRepository: incoming STATIC (confidence 1.0) over existing MUTABLE (0.7) -> update confidence 0.7, result mutability mutable. New-static-fact path still works: with no existing row repo.store is called and the stored fact keeps mutability STATIC and confidence 1.0 (reproduced; the pre-existing existing-static and mutable-update tests also pass). Residual advisory: the update still writes natural_lang_repr and payload from the static observation (the new test pins empty values), so a static observation can change the description/payload of an existing non-static fact without changing confidence; and the new guard uses identity (`fact.mutability is FactMutability.STATIC`), which works for the enum instances the extractor builds but not for a plain string 'static' as returned by PostgresFactRepository._row_to_fact (repository.py:431); use equality/normalization if loaded facts can be re-added. Neither breaks the new-static path.

Provenance spoofing resolved. The extractor now assigns the provenance keys instead of setdefault: source is always set to 'conversation', and session_id is set to the real session whenever one is supplied (conversation_extractor.py:54-56). The new test test_llm_payload_cannot_spoof_provenance feeds an LLM payload of {'source': 'sensor', 'session_id': 'spoofed'} and asserts the stored payload is {'source': 'conversation', 'session_id': str(session_id)} (tests/memory/test_conversation_extractor.py:243-264); it passes. I also ran the extractor end-to-end through a real FactStore with a mock repository and a fake LLM: stored payload was {'source': 'conversation', 'session_id': '<real uuid>', 'object': 'coffee'}, so the spoofed values were overwritten. The four-file regression run was 57 passed; ruff and mypy on the two changed source files pass. Residual for #83: if a caller passes session_id=None, the conditional leaves any LLM-supplied session_id in place (production ExecutionModule always passes one); and the label is 'conversation', not the evidence spec's source_type vocabulary (sensor|user_confirm|llm), so #83 must map the conversation seam to llm or the producer should emit llm. Evidence value is symbolic_repr, so these payload keys do not alter the value hash. The concrete-FactExtractor typing note from the original STD-2 row is unrelated and remains open.
